_comment: Expected state of every upstream pin that xtcp2 depends on for its netlink
tooling, recorded so that drift is visible rather than silent.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. proto-audit — the netlink layout oracle wired up in
nix/checks/proto-audit-netlink.nix — reaches xtcp2 through TWO pins, and
both can go stale independently:
1. xtcp2's own `xdp2` flake input. If xdp2's main moves, we keep
auditing against an older oracle: new NL_* protocols it has learned
about, and fixes to its extractors, never reach us.
2. xdp2's OWN pin of xtcp2 (`xtcp2Rev` in its
nix/proto-audit-sources.nix). This is the one that bites, because it
is proto-audit's DEFAULT for --xtcp2-src. Left at the default, the
oracle audits a GitHub snapshot of xtcp2 from over a year ago and
reports findings about code nobody is running. The oracle check
overrides it to this tree and asserts the override took — see
`stale_note` below for exactly how stale it is.
HOW THIS FILE IS CHECKED. Two halves, because a `nix flake check` sandbox
has no network and so physically cannot ask GitHub whether main has moved:
- nix/checks/upstream-pins.nix (hermetic, in `nix flake check`) asserts
the revs below still match flake.lock and xdp2's own source. It catches
a pin CHANGING without this file being updated.
- `nix run .#check-upstream-pins` (needs network) asks the remotes where
main actually is and reports drift. It catches upstream MOVING. Warns
by default; --strict exits non-zero for CI.
Refresh `rev` here whenever you move a pin, and re-measure the drift
numbers with the runner rather than editing them by recollection.

xdp2.role: Provides proto-audit, the netlink layout oracle.
known_bugs_at_this_rev: samples/proto_audit/src/extractors/xtcp2.rs:143 extract_size_const() builds the pattern `{struct}SizeCst`, but xtcp2 spells these `TCPInfo7_0_3_SizeCst` with an underscore, so no versioned size constant is ever matched and the struct size is inferred from field offsets. Visible as `extract --source xtcp2 --proto NL_Diag_TCPInfo` reporting min_header_bytes 283 rather than 280: 283 is the end of the last unpacked Go field, not the size of the wire struct. Harmless for the oracle, which compares by bit offset and treats min_header_bytes as a minimum.
fixed_at_this_rev: The `.xtcp2("TCPInfo6_10_3")` registry pin in samples/proto_audit/src/name_mapping/table.rs, which made the 11 Accurate ECN fields read as missing from xtcp2. Fixed to `.xtcp2("TCPInfo")` by https://github.com/randomizedcoder/xdp2/pull/11, merged 2026-09-26 as this rev, so resolve_alias() now follows `type TCPInfo TCPInfo7_0_3`. MEASURED across the bump: NL_Diag_TCPInfo goes 76/54/3/8/11 to 80/61/3/16/0 (total/agree/type_differ/mismatch/missing). Note that the fix was NOT 11 missing becoming 11 agreements: the 7 plain __u32 counters became agreements and need no allowlist entry, while the other 4 are members of the packed __u32 at [276:280] and surfaced as 4 kind=split PAIRS - 8 new entries, one per side, at offsets 2208/2210/2212/2216 (kernel, tcpi_*) and 2208/2216/2224/2232 (xtcp2, bare names). Allowlist went 22 -> 19. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo in nix/checks/proto-audit-netlink-allowlist.json.
xdp2.on_bump: Re-run `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.proto-audit-netlink` and read $out/unallowlisted.json before anything else. A proto-audit bump can change what the oracle reports, so it should land on its own rather than inside unrelated work.
xdp2.recheck_on_bump: Rebuild .#checks.x86_64-linux.proto-audit-netlink and read $out/unallowlisted-gated.json, not $out/unallowlisted.json. NL_Diag_TCPInfo is a gated protocol, so a delta there fails the build; the ~179 advisory deltas on the other protocols are expected and do not.

xdp2-embedded-xtcp2.verify_via: grep xtcp2Rev in the xdp2 flake input's source tree
xdp2-embedded-xtcp2.consumed_by: proto-audit itself, whenever --xtcp2-src is NOT overridden
xdp2-embedded-xtcp2.stale_note: Dated 2025-04-19 and 732 commits behind xtcp2 main as of 2026-09-26 — it predates essentially all of the netlink coverage work, including the 7 kernel-versioned TCPInfo variants and the AccECN trailer. Auditing it would re-report the very gap that work closed. This is EXPECTED to be stale and is not a bug to fix here: the fix is that every xtcp2-side proto-audit invocation overrides the path. The runner still reports it so the number cannot quietly grow into something worse without anyone noticing, and so that bumping it upstream is an informed choice rather than a surprise.
